0.label: horned_figure_with_crossed_blades_sun_moon_posts
0.description: The pasted print: a figure with large round eyes and bared teeth under a striped cap with two pointed horns, two long serrated blades crossed over the chest, standing between scalloped posts topped by a disc (left) and a crescent (right), on a scalloped base.
0.iconography: Crossed bands or blades on the chest match the two leaders of the Ado-Ekiti door (#23, #34) and the face on FoA_04-5583. The disc and crescent on the posts may be sun and moon. A warrior or an òrìṣà with horns of power.

panel.title: Mount sheet: a horned figure with crossed blades, between sun and moon posts, from the Modakeke temple board
panel.object_type: archive mount sheet with a printed detail (after Frobenius 1923, pl. 184)
panel.summary: A small print, 'enlarged 2×', of a round-eyed, horned figure with crossed blades between two posts, captioned 'from Plate 184 … partial drawing of a carved temple board, excavated by the D.I.A.F.E. in 1910 at Modeke [Modakeke], Yorubaland'.

register_readings.reading: One figure: horned cap, crossed blades, disc and crescent on the posts.

panel.composition: A frontal figure boxed between two decorated posts on a scalloped base.
panel.narrative: The third figure from the Modakeke board. Where KBA_19153 and 19154 show kings with staffs, this one is armed: crossed blades over the chest, the mark of the war leaders on the Ado-Ekiti door. One board thus held both of the collection's main types — the ruler and the war leader.
panel.hypotheses: Supports both 'chronicle of rulers' and 'war': the same board carries a king type and a warrior type.
uncertainties: The crossed forms could be leaves, whisks or bandoliers rather than blades.
The disc and crescent may be decoration, not sun and moon.
